scenes.title: 1975 Outdoor Oban Scottish Loch Pier: Scuba Divers Comparing Weighted Underwater Formica Slates Against Dry Shore Clipboards
scenes.era: 1975, open-air wooden diving pier & clear tidal loch, Oban, Scotland

layout.description: Crisp sunlit Scottish coastal timber pier jutting over clear turquoise-green loch water: above on dry planks stand Alan Baddeley and Duncan Godden beside dry-suited divers holding wooden clipboards, while down beside the submerged pier ladder hovers a scuba diver at 20-foot depth writing on a weighted white Formica slate.

positions.who: Alan Baddeley & Duncan Godden (researchers in 1975 cream cable-knit wool sweaters and coastal windbreakers)
positions.where: kneeling at the sunlit wooden pier edge feeding the underwater audio headphone cable down into the clear water
positions.facing: looking down toward the submerged diver and across to the shore diver

positions.who: Scottish Scuba Diver (in 1975 black neoprene wetsuit, twin-hose regulator, and yellow air tank)
positions.where: hovering beside the underwater pier pilings gripping a weighted white Formica writing slate and tethered graphite pencil
positions.facing: angled upward toward the sunlit water surface and slate

props.name: weighted white Formica underwater writing slate and tethered graphite pencil
props.period_detail: authentic 1975 waterproof plastic diver slate weighted with lead strip for 20-foot Scottish dives
props.physical_behavior: State-A blank white underwater slate held steady in gloved hand -> State-B diver briskly writes recalled noun rows underwater as air bubbles rise

props.name: pier-side underwater intercom reel and dry wooden clipboard
props.period_detail: 1970s field audio cable drum and weathered oak shore clipboard
props.physical_behavior: State-A researcher unspools audio line down into the loch -> State-B lifts soaked Formica slate beside dry shore clipboard to reveal 13.5 vs 8.6 crossover

actions.verb_sequence: lowers the waterproof audio line off the wooden pier and reads the 36-word list -> pulls up the wet Formica slate to compare side-by-side with the dry shore clipboard
climbs onto dry rock stalling on a nearly blank sheet at 8.4 words -> plunges back underwater and rapidly fills 11.4 words down the Formica slate

reactions.reaction: taps the full underwater Formica slate in disbelief that cold water unlocked the words missing on dry land
points between the wet slate and dry clipboard confirming the 46% matched-context jump

scenes.wardrobe: 1975 Scottish coastal fieldwork: chunky cream fisherman sweaters and navy windbreakers; vintage black neoprene wetsuits, oval dive masks, and yellow scuba cylinders.
scenes.lighting: Bright crisp Highland coastal daylight sparkling across timber pier planks and clear teal water.
scenes.recognition_hook: Learn 36 words twenty feet underwater: dry on the sunny beach you stall at 8.4 words, jump back into the cold water and 11.4 words rush back.

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1975 Scottish wooden diving pier where researchers in cable-knit sweaters compare dry shore clipboards with a scuba diver's weighted white underwater Formica slate

scenes.title: 1980 Oban Pier Follow-Up: Multiple-Choice Recognition Erases the Land-Water Gap

layout.description: Outdoor weathered timber table on the Oban pier where wetsuits dry in the breeze beside printed multiple-choice word checklists.

positions.where: standing at the pier table circling printed recognition words briskly with zero hesitation after climbing out of the water

props.name: printed multiple-choice recognition slate and red wax pencil
props.period_detail: 1980 waterproof checklist contrasting directly with 1975 blank free-recall slates
props.physical_behavior: State-A diver climbs onto dry pier dripping water -> State-B circles recognized words rapidly down the checklist with zero context loss

actions.verb_sequence: pushes dive mask onto forehead, picks up the red wax pencil, and circles target words down the recognition sheet without stalling

reactions.reaction: nods seeing recognition scores match evenly across land and water

scenes.wardrobe: Half-unzipped neoprene wetsuit over wool jersey; coastal windbreaker.
scenes.recognition_hook: Swap the blank slate for a multiple-choice sheet, and the entire underwater-versus-shore memory gap drops to zero.

scenes.title: Hardware Store Aisle Reset: Picturing Your Home Garage Workbench for 20 Seconds
scenes.era: Modern Saturday morning neighborhood hardware store aisle

layout.description: Bright hardware store fastener aisle where a 52-year-old homeowner stands holding two brass hinges, pausing to remember the third needed item.

positions.where: standing beside bins of screws, closing eyes briefly for twenty seconds to picture their home garage workbench, then reaching straight for wood glue

props.name: woven red hardware basket and brass cabinet hinges
props.physical_behavior: State-A homeowner pauses over half-empty basket -> State-B closes eyes twenty seconds, snaps eyes open, and drops the missing bottle cleanly into the basket

actions.verb_sequence: stops in the aisle staring at two hinges -> closes eyes for twenty seconds picturing the garage bench -> reaches up and grabs the exact bottle off the shelf

reactions.reaction: grins with quiet relief as mental room reinstatement unlocks the missing third item

scenes.wardrobe: Casual weekend flannel overshirt and khaki trousers.
scenes.recognition_hook: You don't need to drive back home—twenty seconds of picturing your garage bench hands your brain the missing room key.
